page.layout: One printed page, one column of numbered questions. Questions 11 to 18 run above a centred heading "MEDICA", followed by questions 19 to 26. No margin notes, running head or page number.

main_text.p: 11. Cur Lunam, quæ in sphæra faciem conglobatur, rec-tam cum δίχοτομος[?] fit, cernamus?
12. Cur, si intra aquam pedem quis teneat calidam, pede quiescente, aqua minus calida sentiat, movente calidiore?
13. Quam ob causam manu præ lucerna, aut Sole obiecta, melius inspicere possimus?
14. Cur ◡[?]Aqua puteorum per hyemem calida, per æstatem vero frigida sit?
15. Cur genus sylvestrium stirpium validius & latius esse soleat, quam urbanum, etiam Hippocrati.
16. Cur sensus quinq; tantum, non plures, neq; pauciores habeamus?
18. Qua de causa Sol hominem nigrum reddat, linteum candidum faciat; & ceram deniq; emolliat, lutum induret?
main_text.head: MEDICA.
main_text.p: 19. Quam ob causam homines, qui ex ardua febre in-saniunt, robustissimi quandiu insaniunt, sint; soluti autē insaniâ, admodum debilitentur, & langueant?
20. Cur Febrium Accessiones certo venire ordine so-leant?
21. Quam ob causam, qui febriunt, plus sitiant, quam fa-me affligantur; qui conualescunt, plus famescant, quam sitiant?
22. Quare multi ◡[?]Medicorum existiment risum ex-Liene exoriri?
23. Cur itidem dolores per noctem magis soleant au-geri?
24. Cur qui regio laborant morbo, adstricta sint aluo; excrementaq; admodum alba egerant?
25. Quam ob causam, qui aqua intercute laborât, as-siduè[?] sitiant; cùm tamen aquâ sint admodum pleni?

page.notes: The Greek word in question 11 (δίχοτομος) is read with doubt; the accent and the first letters are unclear. The sign ◡ before "Aqua" (14) and "Medicorum" (22) is an unidentified mark, not a letter; it is copied as a curved symbol with [?]. The word in 25 before "sitiant" is unclear at the start, as is the line-end hyphen after "as-". The catchword "Cur" at the foot belongs to question 26, which is printed there as "26. Cur". Hyphens at line ends (re-ctam, in-saniunt, so-leant, fa-me, ex-Liene, au-geri) are printed hyphens kept as in the scan.
